stories.headline: Putin tells Witkoff he will resume three-way Ukraine peace talks after Nov. 10; US detainee freed

key_facts.fact: Vladimir Putin agreed 'in principle' on Wednesday, Oct. 21, to resume trilateral negotiations with the US and Ukraine after Nov. 10, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said after Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed Wednesday to resume three-way negotiations next month with Washington and Kyiv aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, a Kremlin official said. The Russian leader has agreed "in principle" to resume the talks after Nov. 10

key_facts.fact: The meeting lasted about three hours; Witkoff presented an updated proposal to end the war and Jared Kushner joined virtually. Ushakov said the talks could take place in Abu Dhabi.
key_facts.excerpt: During a three-hour meeting in St. Petersburg, Witkoff presented Putin with an updated proposal to end the war in Ukraine. Trump envoy Jared Kushner joined virtually. ... adding that the talks could take place in Abu Dhabi.

key_facts.fact: Before the meeting Russia released US citizen Stephen Hubbard, 74, held for more than four years after being seized in eastern Ukraine in April 2022; Witkoff called Putin 'a humanitarian', drawing criticism from Republican senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia released U.S. citizen Stephen Hubbard, 74, who had spent more than four years in captivity after being seized by Russian troops in eastern Ukraine in April 2022. ... Witkoff in response thanked Putin and called him "a humanitarian." Sens. John Cornyn (R-Texas) and Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) expressed outrage

key_facts.fact: Ushakov said the Ukrainian and European proposals Witkoff brought from Oslo 'contained little that was useful' for resolving the crisis.
key_facts.excerpt: the proposals brought to St. Petersburg by Witkoff, which he attributed to Ukraine and the European Union, "contained little that was useful in the context of resolving the Ukrainian crisis."

key_facts.fact: A day earlier in Oslo, Zelenskyy said US early-warning intelligence on Russian ballistic missiles had been restored after meeting Witkoff with the leaders of Finland and Norway.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy confirming that crucial US early-warning intelligence on Russian ballistic missiles had been restored and that Washington had reaffirmed its commitment to strong security guarantees for Ukraine after the war.

key_facts.fact: Zelenskyy told Fox News on Oct. 21 he is open to freezing the current front lines as a way to end the war: 'Yes, right now, we have to freeze.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Yes, right now, we have to freeze," Zelenskyy responded. "And I think this is [a] real way to end this war."

key_facts.fact: The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February, before the US and Israel launched a war against Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February before the United States and Israel launched a war against Iran.

stories.headline: WSJ: Musk ordered Ukraine's Starshield slowdown; Rubio says access is SpaceX's call, not White House

key_facts.fact: The Wall Street Journal reported on Oct. 20 that Elon Musk ordered the slowdown of Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink that Ukraine relies on, citing US officials and people familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday that Musk had ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of Starlink that Ukraine relies on to defend itself against missile attacks from Russia.

key_facts.fact: Musk capped the speed at which Ukrainian equipment could connect to the system, making some of Kyiv's drones useless, according to the Journal; Musk had earlier said any limits were 'decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS'.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk capped the speed at which Ukrainian equipment could connect to the system, making some of Kyiv's drones useless, the Journal reported ... Musk had previously said that "any limits on speed or usage" of Starshield systems were "decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,"

key_facts.fact: The WSJ cited one source saying Musk, Trump and White House officials discussed the matter beforehand, and two sources saying Musk and Trump discussed it in the days after the slowdown.
key_facts.excerpt: The Journal cited one source saying that Musk, President Donald Trump and White House officials discussed the matter beforehand, and two sources saying that Musk and the president discussed the matter in the days after the slowdown.

key_facts.fact: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in India on Oct. 21 that Ukraine's Starlink access is governed by a private commercial contract and that he was not aware Washington knew of the decision beforehand.
key_facts.excerpt: "I'm not aware that we knew about this decision beforehand. But that's irrelevant," Rubio told reporters during a trip to India. "The bottom line is that that is governed by a private commercial contract as to how their stuff can be used and what speeds they'll allow it to be used at."

key_facts.fact: Reuters had previously cited two US officials and a Western official saying the decision came from the White House, a version the administration denies.
key_facts.excerpt: Reuters has cited two US officials and a Western official briefed on the matter saying the decision ultimately came from the White House. This version was also asserted by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, but denied by the administration.

key_facts.fact: Zelenskyy said on Oct. 21 that Ukraine's access to Starshield data remained 'limited' but that Rubio was working on restoring full access.
key_facts.excerpt: access to data from the Starshield satellite network, the military version of Elon Musk's Starlink system, remained "limited" in Ukraine, but that Rubio was working on it and expected full access to be restored.

stories.headline: Tankers hit off Oman and Iraq as Iran rebuffs Pakistan-mediated talks with the US

key_facts.fact: An unknown projectile struck a tanker 11 nautical miles west of Oman's Bukha, overlooking the Strait of Hormuz, on Wednesday, Oct. 21; a fire was extinguished and all crew were reported safe, UKMTO said.
key_facts.excerpt: An unknown projectile struck a tanker 11 nautical miles west of Oman's Bukha, which overlooks the Strait of Hormuz, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Wednesday. UKMTO said a fire that erupted was extinguished and that the tanker was at anchor.

key_facts.fact: UKMTO also reported a tanker struck by a projectile on Tuesday 30 nautical miles southeast of Al Faw, Iraq, in the northern Persian Gulf, with no damage reported.
key_facts.excerpt: "The master of a tanker reports being struck by an unknown projectile, the crew are reported as safe and there is no reported damage or environmental impact," the UKMTO's advisory said. The incident took place 30 nautical miles southeast of Al Faw, Iraq

key_facts.fact: Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei told visiting Pakistani army chief Asim Munir there will be no negotiations until the US meets Iran's seven conditions and that 'not even a tiny bit' of enriched nuclear material will leave Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: "Not even a tiny bit of enriched nuclear material will leave Iran ..." ... "There will be no negotiations until America takes steps to build trust - a process that must begin with the fulfilment of Iran's conditions," he added.

key_facts.fact: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran presented a seven-day initiative under which the Strait of Hormuz would fully reopen on the sixth day, and that the strait stays closed unless Washington accepts Tehran's conditions.
key_facts.excerpt: Araghchi told Iraq's Al Ekhbariya television that Iran had presented a seven-day initiative under which the strategic waterway would fully reopen on the sixth day.

key_facts.fact: IRGC commander Yadollah Javani warned Iran could target seven undersea internet cables running through the Strait of Hormuz if the US resumes attacks.
key_facts.excerpt: Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander Brig. Gen. Yadollah Javani warned that Iran could target seven critical undersea internet cables passing through the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. resumes attacks on Iran.

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs said on Oct. 20 the global average crude freight rate has surged above $20 per barrel, from $3 a year earlier, as attacks near Hormuz drive up shipping costs.
key_facts.excerpt: The global average crude freight rate has surged above $20 per barrel, compared with just $3 a year earlier, according to a Goldman Sachs report published Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: Brent reached $111.99 intraday on Oct. 20, its highest in five months, before settling at $108.79; WTI settled 1.8% lower at $101.79.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude reached $111.99 a barrel intraday, its highest level in five months, before reversing and settling 0.69% lower at $108.79. West Texas Intermediate settled 1.8% lower at $101.79.

key_facts.fact: At least 23 incidents involving ships attacked in or near Hormuz were logged in the first two weeks of October, at least five with engine-room impacts, as Iran shifts to using more missiles than drones.
key_facts.excerpt: At least 23 incidents involving ships attacked in or near the Strait of Hormuz were logged in the first two weeks of October, with at least five reporting impacts to their engine rooms

stories.headline: FDA approves GSK's Hibsago, first antisense drug for chronic hepatitis B, aiming at functional cure

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved GSK's Hibsago (bepirovirsen) on Oct. 20, 2026, in combination with existing antiviral therapy, for chronic hepatitis B in certain adults without cirrhosis; it is the first FDA-approved antisense oligonucleotide for the disease.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) injection, in combination with existing antiviral therapy, to treat chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in certain adults without cirrhosis. Hibsago is the first FDA-approved antisense oligonucleotide to treat chronic hepatitis B.

key_facts.fact: Eligible patients must have taken antiviral therapy for at least six months, have suppressed viral levels and HBsAg levels of 3,000 IU/mL or less; Hibsago is injected under the skin for up to 24 weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: approved for certain adults without cirrhosis who have been taking HBV antiviral therapy for at least six months, have suppressed levels of HBV in their blood and have hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) levels of 3,000 IU/mL or less ... Hibsago is injected under the skin for up to 24 weeks.

key_facts.fact: Across two trials, 24% of Hibsago patients met requirements to stop their existing medicine versus none on placebo; 24 weeks after stopping all treatment, 19% still had the virus under control with undetectable HBsAg.
key_facts.excerpt: Across the two trials, 24% of patients who received Hibsago met the requirements to stop their existing medicine, compared with none who received placebo. Twenty-four weeks after stopping all hepatitis B treatment, 19% of patients who received Hibsago still had the virus under control

key_facts.fact: GSK says standard of care typically achieves less than 1% functional cure after one year, and chronic hepatitis B affects about 1.7 million people in the US.
key_facts.excerpt: functional cure rates of 19% in adults with ≤3000 IU/ml HBsAg, compared to current standard of care alone, which typically achieves less than 1% functional cure rate after one year of treatment ... CHB affects approximately 1.7 million people in the US

key_facts.fact: Hibsago carries a boxed warning for serious liver reactions and low platelet counts that can raise the risk of life-threatening bleeding.
key_facts.excerpt: Hibsago has a boxed warning for serious liver reactions as well as low platelet counts, which can increase the risk of potentially life-threatening bleeding.

key_facts.fact: Hibsago is the FDA's 47th novel drug approval of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: 47. | Hibsago | bepirovirsen | 10/20/2026 | To treat chronic hepatitis B virus infection in certain adults without cirrhosis

stories.headline: SpaceX posts $14.6B Q3 revenue and $4.4B profit; Musk says Tesla merger committees formed

key_facts.fact: SpaceX reported Q3 2026 revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161% from $5.6 billion, net income of $4.4 billion versus a $1.1 billion loss a year earlier, and adjusted EBITDA of $8.8 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenues of $14.6 billion, up 161% from $5.6 billion • Net income of $4.4 billion, an improvement of $5.5 billion from net loss of $1.1 billion • Adjusted EBITDA of $8.8 billion, up 306% from $2.2 billion

key_facts.fact: Segment revenue: Space $1.77 billion, Connectivity (Starlink) $5.25 billion, up 69% year over year, and Super Intelligence (SI) $7.56 billion, up 830%; Starlink reached 13.6 million consumer subscribers.
key_facts.excerpt: Space | $1,767 ... Connectivity | 5,248 ... SI | 7,560 ... reached 13.6 million Starlink consumer subscribers, up 1.6 million sequentially

key_facts.fact: SpaceX flew its first revenue-generating Starship mission, delivering 26 Starlink V3 satellites, and quarterly capex reached $19.6 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Successfully launched our first revenue-generating Starship mission, delivering 26 Starlink V3 satellites to our broadband constellation ... Total | $19,593

key_facts.fact: On the Oct. 20 earnings call Musk said SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees of independent directors to discuss a potential merger, that he supports the idea, and that no agreement on terms has been reached.
key_facts.excerpt: "The special committees have not reached an agreement of the terms of any transaction and there is no guarantee that they will but I do think there is a lot of merit in combining the companies," Musk said Tuesday on SpaceX's quarterly earnings conference call.

key_facts.fact: Musk said any deal would need approval from a majority of all outstanding Tesla shares, 'quite a high hurdle', and called the process 'an odd kabuki dance' in which he cannot take part.
key_facts.excerpt: "It is an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking and I cannot be in the conversation," Musk said. ... approval would need a majority of all outstanding shares—not merely a majority of shares voted—creating what he called "quite a high hurdle."

key_facts.fact: SpaceX guided Q4 capex of $35-40 billion and Q1 2027 revenue of $33-37 billion, and reported a $63 billion backlog.
key_facts.excerpt: The company now expects $35 billion to $40 billion in capital expenditures in the fourth quarter ... First quarter 2027 revenue will be $33-$37 billion ... it had $63 billion in backlog

key_facts.fact: SpaceX shares rose more than 8% after Musk's comments while Tesla added 2.4%; JPMorgan analysts see a likely SpaceX-led all-stock deal.
key_facts.excerpt: "We see the potential deal structure as likely to be a SPCX-led all-stock deal ..." JPMorgan analysts said ... SpaceX shares spiked by more than 8% following Musk's comments, while Tesla added 2.4%.

stories.headline: French-German 10-year spread closes at widest since 2011 amid unrest and budget fight

key_facts.fact: The gap between French and German 10-year yields closed at 1.53 percentage points on Oct. 20, its highest close since 2011.
key_facts.excerpt: à 1,53 point, l'écart entre les taux français et allemand à dix ans atteint son plus haut niveau en clôture depuis 2011

key_facts.fact: The spread touched 156 basis points in the early afternoon of Oct. 20; the French 10-year yield reached 4.98% before closing at 4.92%, while the Italy-Germany spread stood at 112.
key_facts.excerpt: è salito sopra la soglia dei 150 punti ed è arrivato nel primo pomeriggio fino a quota 156 ... il rendimento dei titoli di Stato francesi è arrivato al 4,98% ... per poi ripiegare e chiudere al 4,92%

key_facts.fact: French OAT yields remained near 24-year highs after their biggest daily rise in nearly a month, as protest groups called for further demonstrations after weekend unrest; the early-October peak of 4.9937% was the highest since July 2002.
key_facts.excerpt: French government bond yields remained near 24-year highs on Tuesday after their biggest daily rise in nearly a month ... French protestor groups called for further demonstrations after last weekend's unrest ... the early October peak of 4.9937%, which was the most since July 2002.

key_facts.fact: The cost of insuring French debt via five-year credit default swaps hovered near 79 basis points, its highest since 2013.
key_facts.excerpt: The cost of insuring Parisian debt against default via five-year credit default swaps (CDS) hovered near 79.05 basis points - its highest level since the 2013 sovereign debt crisis.

key_facts.fact: ECB Governing Council member Olli Rehn said French spreads had widened 'somewhat' due to global and country-specific factors.
key_facts.excerpt: French bond spreads relative to German bunds have widened "somewhat" as a result of both global and country-specific factors, European Central Bank Governing Council member Olli Rehn said.

key_facts.fact: The sell-off comes six months before France's presidential election, while parliament debates the 2027 budget after a weekend of violence and looting during cost-of-living protests.
key_facts.excerpt: A sei mesi dalle elezioni presidenziali francesi ... in seguito a un fine settimana segnato da violenze, devastazioni e saccheggi nel Paese a margine delle manifestazioni contro il carovita e mentre il Parlamento discute la manovra finanziaria 2027.

stories.headline: eBay to cut about 9% of staff, roughly 1,100 jobs, in its second layoff round of 2026

key_facts.fact: eBay will lay off about 9% of its workforce to simplify operations and shift resources to its fastest-growing areas, CEO Jamie Iannone told staff in a memo reviewed by Reuters; an eBay spokesperson confirmed the cuts on Oct. 21.
key_facts.excerpt: EBay will lay off about 9% of its workforce as the online marketplace looks to simplify operations and shift resources to its fastest-growing areas, CEO Jamie Iannone told staff in a memo that was reviewed by Reuters. A spokesperson for eBay confirmed the layoffs to Reuters on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: The cut eliminates around 1,100 jobs based on eBay's 12,300 employees at end-2025; eBay already cut about 6%, or 800 employees, in February.
key_facts.excerpt: The move will eliminate around 1,100 jobs, based on the 12,300 employees eBay had at the end of last year. The company also let go about 6% of its workforce, or 800 employees, in February

key_facts.fact: Iannone wrote 'Our strategy is working' and that capturing the opportunity ahead requires 'thoughtful choices about where we focus and invest'; affected staff will be told in the coming days.
key_facts.excerpt: "Our strategy is working," Iannone said in the memo, adding that "continuing to capture the significant opportunity ahead requires us to make thoughtful choices about where we focus and invest." He said affected staff would be informed in the coming days.

key_facts.fact: eBay shares have risen nearly 40% this year versus about 12% for the S&P 500, helped by authenticated luxury, collectibles, refurbished goods and its $1.4 billion purchase of Depop.
key_facts.excerpt: That has helped its shares rise nearly 40% this year, outperforming the benchmark S&P 500's around 12% gain. ... its $1.4 billion deal for fashion resale platform Depop

key_facts.fact: eBay employs about 1,000 people in Ireland and is set to report earnings next week.
key_facts.excerpt: EBay has an Irish workforce of about 1,000. ... The company is slated to report latest earnings next week.
